meta.title: Operation of Laminar Air Flow Cabinet in Microbiology Laboratory

sections.purpose: To provide a sterile working environment with HEPA-filtered unidirectional air flow for aseptic manipulation of microbiological cultures, preparation of sterile culture media, and sterility testing of pharmaceutical products.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Microbiology laboratory for all aseptic operations including transfer of microbial cultures, sterility testing, antimicrobial sensitivity disc preparation, and reconstitution of parenteral samples for sterility testing.
procedure: Switch on the blower (fan) of the LAF cabinet at least 15–20 minutes before use to allow the HEPA filter to establish unidirectional air flow and purge any particulates.
Simultaneously switch on the UV lamp for 15–20 minutes to decontaminate the work surface — ensure no personnel are present in the room during UV exposure.
Switch OFF the UV lamp before entering the room or beginning work — UV radiation causes severe eye and skin injury.
Put on clean lab coat, gloves, mask, and hair cover before approaching the cabinet.
Wipe the work surface of the LAF cabinet with a 70% isopropyl alcohol-dampened, lint-free wipe — wipe from back to front in a single motion.
Allow the alcohol to evaporate completely (30–60 seconds) before placing materials inside.
Arrange all required materials (cultures, media, pipettes, loops) in the cabinet before starting to minimize arm movements in and out during the procedure.
Work at least 15 cm inside the cabinet front opening — the air curtain at the front opening is the critical containment barrier.
Flame all loops and instruments before and after each use if using an open flame (use a micro-incinerator inside the LAF to avoid disrupting air flow).
Avoid excessive arm movements across the work zone — lateral movements disrupt laminar flow.
Perform all aseptic manipulations with deliberate, slow movements.
After use, remove all materials; wipe the work surface with 70% isopropyl alcohol.
Allow the blower to run for 5 minutes after work is completed before switching off.
Log each use: date, operator, procedures performed, and any incidents in the LAF usage register.
precautions: Never use the LAF cabinet as a biosafety cabinet (BSC) for handling pathogenic organisms — LAF protects the product, not the operator. BSC is required for biological hazards.
Switch off the UV lamp before entering the work area — UV causes photokeratitis (eye damage) and skin burns.
Do not obstruct the rear grille — blocking air intake breaks laminar flow.
Do not work at the very front edge — the air curtain is weaker at the front and contamination can enter.
Replace HEPA filters when airflow velocity drops below 0.45 m/s or per manufacturer's schedule.
Validate the LAF cabinet annually with particle count testing and airflow velocity measurement.
Do not use aerosol-generating sprays inside the LAF — they disrupt laminar flow and deposit on HEPA filter.
